page.message: for="does-not-exist" points at the id "does-not-exist", which does not exist on the page. The screen reader loses the label. Write for on the label and id on the field in the template, or put the label around the field. If the code that renders the markup can call a builder function, lt.field({ id }) or Lt.field(id = ...) does it.

<input> has no label: no <label for> pointing at it, no <label> around it, and no aria-label or aria-labelledby. A screen reader announces the field without a name. Write for on the label and id on the field in the template, or put the label around the field. If the code that renders the markup can call a builder function, lt.field({ id }) or Lt.field(id = ...) does it.

aria-describedby="budget-help nowhere" points at the id "nowhere", which does not exist on the page. The screen reader loses the description. Write that id on the text that describes this element, or take it out of aria-describedby.
id="budget-help" appears more than once on the page. aria-describedby points at the first of them. Every id must be unique.
for="total-from" points at the id "total-from", which does not exist on the page. The <output> is then not tied to the field it shows the result of. Write that id on the field, or take it out of for.
id="lone" appears more than once on the page. Anything that points at it reaches the first one. Every id must be unique.
